recommended_title: Is Grokking Delay Width-Dependent? A Censoring-Aware Seed-Cluster Slope Test on Modular Addition Finds No Resolvable Trend
central_question: In a one-layer transformer trained with AdamW on modular addition (p=97, train fraction 0.4, weight decay 1.0, full batch, 10,000-step limit), does the delay between fitting the training set and generalizing decrease with model width, as a pre-registered seed-cluster slope test can detect?
central_thesis: Under a strictly specified and evaluator-owned protocol, the log-delay vs log2-width slope is -0.020 with a 95% seed-cluster bootstrap CI of [-0.585, 0.354] (4 seeds x 5 widths, 40% of runs censored at the step limit), so the 'delay decreases with width' prediction is neither supported nor refuted; the paper's contribution is a calibrated negative/inconclusive measurement, a censoring-aware test design whose resolution limits are made explicit, and a clear list of what the evidence cannot say.
narrative_rationale: The sealed final evaluation completed with outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome, status completed, correct true), so a paper about the measured results is supported. But 'qualified' certifies that the evaluation ran validly; it does not say the width hypothesis was supported. The decision rule fixed by the task contract (CI entirely below zero = supported, at/above zero = refuted, straddling = inconclusive) yields 'inconclusive' because the CI straddles zero. That is the most defensible and most honest story: a measurement-resolution paper. Alternatives rejected: (a) capacity-crossover / critical-width story (P1-P3 of the first model variant) -- no t_mem, t_gen, width-by-fraction or d*(f) results exist in the grounded artifacts; (b) lazy-to-rich or effective-learning-rate confound explanation -- the hidden-layer reparametrization sweep script was written but never executed (no code executed in that stage), so no evidence compares reparametrization strengths; (c) 'best search score = winner' story -- scores come from a different data plane, 2 seeds, and an undisclosed score formula; they cannot support a width claim. The retained claim is therefore narrow: what the final test measured and how little it resolves.
edit_framing_decision: Not in edit mode: no previous_paper directory or edit context exists; a fresh framing was produced. Marked 'rejected' only to mean no prior story is carried over.
staged_input_impact: No staged prior manuscript or new staged program present; no downstream_study block in paper_data.json. The framing relies on final_evaluation, the three search-phase model variants (grounding ids result.*), and the evaluator task contract/manifest staged under task/.

method_groups.name: Evaluated width-scaled one-layer transformer (frozen final model variant)
method_groups.include_reason: The single model variant that was run in the sealed final evaluation (last-position-only forward, init scale 0.5, width-aware output scaling exponent 0.5 and hidden-layer reparametrization exponent 0.5 relative to reference width 128). It is the object of every final number; describe exactly its code-level constants.

method_groups.include_reason: Provides final.metric.reference_delay_log_slope = -0.368 from the first final seed only (single seed, no CI). Use as a cross-check comparator, not as a significance claim; the paper must not attribute the gap to -0.020 to the reparametrization because that was not isolated.

method_groups.name: Held-out control episodes (no-signal control)
method_groups.include_reason: final.metric.control_max_val_acc = 0.0122 shows the evaluation does not trivially produce high validation accuracy under the control; supports measurement validity. Describe what the control is only as far as the task contract states it; otherwise mark unknown.

method_groups.name: Search-phase model variants (three nested configurations)
method_groups.include_reason: Three configurations were each evaluated once on 2 search seeds (101,102): initial capacity-sweep configuration, + width-aware output scaling, + hidden-layer reparametrization. Their scores (0.798, 0.828, 0.850) and censored fractions (0.667, 1.0, 0.667) can be shown as a descriptive design-history table in a compact form, explicitly separated from final results, with 2 seeds and an undisclosed score formula; no causal attribution.

results_focus: Primary: final slope of ln(delay) vs log2(width) = -0.0198 with seed-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [-0.5846, 0.3542] (2000 resamples, 4 seeds, 5 widths 16-256), decision = inconclusive under the pre-declared rule; evaluator reference slope -0.3676 (single seed) lies inside the CI.

Censoring: 40% of final primary runs censored (final.metric.censored_fraction = 0.4), with censored and floored delays kept at declared worst-case/floor values; the delay metric is bounded between one probe interval (250 steps) and the 10,000-step limit, so (derived from these manifest values) log-gap range is at most ln(40)~3.69 and the slope over 4 doublings of width is bounded in magnitude by ~0.92; the CI covers a large part of this range. Present as a resolution analysis.
Validity checks: missing_episodes = 0, control_max_val_acc = 0.0122; qualification outcome 'qualified' (status completed, correct true). State diagnostics beyond these as unknown.

Seed-level spread: four final episodes with evaluator seed scores 0.607, 0.733, 0.717, 0.860 (mean 0.729); the score formula is not visible, so describe only as seed-to-seed variability of an evaluator summary score, not as performance. Avoid the internal metric name in visible text.

Search-phase descriptive table (separate from final): three configurations, 2 seeds each, scores/censoring; note that score ordering is not monotone with censoring (c02 has censored fraction 1.0 yet higher score than c01), which shows the summary score cannot be read as a grokking-speed measure.

Not available (state explicitly): per-width and per-seed delay values, t_mem/t_gen separately, critical width d*(f), train-fraction sweeps, the HIDDEN_EXP {0,0.5,1} sweep, weight-decay equalization control. These were proposed but have no executed results.
figure_plan: Fig 1 (overview, early, page 1-2): concept schematic of the evaluation protocol and decision rule: width list -> train one-layer transformer at fixed AdamW settings -> checkpoint probes every 250 steps -> delay gap (first >=99% val minus first >=99% train, floored at 250, censored at 10,000) -> OLS slope of ln gap vs log2 width -> seed-cluster bootstrap CI -> three-way verdict (CI<0 supported / straddles 0 inconclusive / >=0 refuted); highlight where this run's CI lands.

Fig 2 (main result): single-panel interval plot on a slope axis: point estimate with 95% CI for the candidate, the reference-trainer point, a vertical zero line, shaded decision regions, and the +/-0.92 attainable-slope bound.
Fig 3 (optional, supplement or small main panel): search-phase configurations with per-seed points for score and censored fraction (2 panels), clearly labeled 'search phase, 2 seeds, not final'.

forbidden_phrases: we discovered that wider models grok faster
wider models memorize faster (as a finding)
notes_for_writer: Final outcome is 'qualified' with status completed (final.qualification.*). Say what that means narrowly (valid, completed evaluation); do not let it imply the width hypothesis was supported. The hypothesis verdict is inconclusive because the CI straddles zero. Gate diagnostics beyond the listed final.qualification.* values are unknown; say so rather than speculating.

Do not claim a width effect in either direction. Point slope -0.020, CI [-0.585, 0.354]; reference single-seed slope -0.368 sits inside the CI; do not claim the reparametrization caused the difference between them.

Censoring and floor: 40% censored; slope is a statistic of a bounded delay metric. Discuss how censoring at 10,000 steps (and floor at 250) compresses and bounds slopes; sensitivity to the step limit was not run. Say that censored values were kept at worst-case values per the task contract.

Only 4 seeds: the cluster bootstrap over 4 clusters is coarse (few distinct resamples); state this as a limitation of the interval, and that CI width (~0.94 slope units) is the main finding on resolution.

Per-width delays are not in grounded artifacts. Do not draw per-width curves, do not report t_mem/t_gen, critical width, or training-fraction effects. Do not report the selected-model search scores as performance on the task question.

Separate search from final: search used seeds 101-102 on a search data plane; final used seeds 201-204 on a sealed plane. Search score ordering is a descriptive context table only; the score formula is not public and its ordering is not monotone with censoring.

Visible terms: use 'seeded run', 'model variant', 'configuration', 'evaluator summary score' (not combined_score). If a thresholded rate is shown, call it 'censored-run fraction' (fraction of runs with no >=99% validation accuracy within 10,000 steps) with one meaning throughout.

Related work: cite only keys present in references.bib: Power2022GrokkingGB, Nanda2023ProgressMF, Liu2022OmnigrokGB, Kumar2023GrokkingAT, Huang2024UnifiedVO (circuit-competition view of grokking/double descent), Lyle2024NormalizationAE and Nam2024DecouplingDR only if their relevance (effective learning rate; dynamical richness) is stated accurately. Several starter references (e.g. circuit efficiency, double descent, AdamW) are not in references.bib; do not cite them unless added. Several bib entries are unrelated noise (e.g. biochemistry, solar cells) and must not be cited.

Positioning: frame as a measurement-resolution and negative-result contribution; motivate mechanistically why width could matter (memorization speed vs generalization time scale; effective step size under AdamW) as hypotheses whose separation this study could not execute, not as established.

Body-page use (8-9 pages, ICLR single column): ~1.2 pages intro+question+contribution list; ~0.8 related work; ~2 pages protocol and model variant (delay definition, censoring, estimator, decision rule, frozen model constants); ~2 pages results (main slope figure, censoring and resolution analysis, validity checks, reference comparison); ~1 page discussion of what could and could not be concluded, alternative explanations (censoring ceiling, 4 seeds, reparametrization confound, single operation/prime); ~0.7 page limitations and scope. Fill with analysis, not padding; if the body is short, add the resolution-bound analysis and a descriptive seed-level table in main text rather than repeating text.

Contributions must be verifiable: (1) a pre-declared, censoring-aware slope test with seed-cluster bootstrap and explicit three-way verdict; (2) a completed measurement on mod-97 addition with the stated outcome; (3) a derived resolution bound explaining why the test is weak here; (4) an explicit inventory of untested explanations.
Anonymous submission: no author names, repository links or environment paths; LLM usage section required.
The only high-level overview figure uses generate-concept-figure; all other figures use matplotlib; export PDF plus 300 DPI PNG and reference the PDF in LaTeX.
